subject: Throughput guardrails & surge protection pricing for Nimbus Health
content:
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: James Liu <james.liu@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Throughput guardrails & surge protection pricing for Nimbus Health

Hi James —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our call, I wanted to nail down a concise proposal for Dedicated capacity + the optional surge protection add-on so your procurement team can budget. High-level:

- Reserved commit: customer pins a GPU pool (vGPU slots) for predictable throughput and a per-minute baseline SLO.
- Surge protection (add-on): short-lived overlay capacity to handle traffic spikes without pre-warming dedicated headroom. Priced as "surge units" (per-second billing aggregated per hour) with a cooldown to avoid persistent overage.

Questions for you so we can finalize the pricing sheet:
1) Do you need a hard dollar cap on surge spend or is a percentage-over-commit cap OK?
2) Preferred cooldown window: many customers pick 10–30 minutes; any constraints from your finance/ops team?
3) Throughput guarantee target (p50/p95 latency goals) for the baseline pool so we can size the vGPU commit.

Attached is an updated pricing worksheet that maps commit sizes to expected token/sec throughput and gives a couple of packaging options (slab surge pricing vs linear per-minute surge billing). Marcus added a recommended guardrail that automatically pauses surge after X consecutive minutes above the commit threshold — that prevents runaway charges but still lets you absorb short bursts.

If you prefer, we can ship a short pilot: 3-month reserved commit with a negotiated surge cap and an immediate on-call contact for incidents.

Look forward to your notes.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0124

Attachment: redwood_dedicated_pricing_sheet_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)
Attachment: Nimbus_DPA.pdf (PDF)

-----
From: James Liu <james.liu@nimbushealth.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Malhotra <priya.m@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput guardrails & surge protection pricing for Nimbus Health

Laura —

Thanks. A few notes from procurement & platform ops:

- We need a hard monthly cap for surge costs that we can commit to in the PO. Prefer a tiered cap (e.g., $X/mo baseline, $Y/mo absolute ceiling) so finance can forecast.
- Cooldown: 15 minutes is our preference, but we also want an override window so platform engineers can temporarily raise it for product launches.
- Throughput: baseline pool should be sized to meet p95 latency <= 350ms for our 512-token median prompt. Can you confirm the vGPU-to-p95 mapping in the sheet?

Also: are there any automatic fallback options if surge capacity is exhausted (e.g., degraded model variant or rate-limited responses)? We need predictable behavior rather than silent failures.

-James
James Liu
Head of Platform Engineering
Nimbus Health
james.liu@nimbushealth.com

-----
On Sep 2, 2026, at 11:44 AM, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai> wrote:

> Hi James —
> 
> Quick technical note to clarify options and guardrails:
> 
> 1) Hard monthly cap: we can enforce a spend ceiling at the account level. If the ceiling is hit, we offer three configurable behaviors: a) block surge requests, b) degrade to a cheaper quantized model variant, or c) throttle to the baseline qps until the next billing window.
> 
> 2) Cooldown and overrides: cooldown is a rolling window measured per pool. The 15-minute default is sensible. We expose an "override token" that Platform Engineers (with MFA) can use to temporarily increase the cooldown or allow N additional surge minutes for a release. Overrides are logged to the audit trail for compliance.
> 
> 3) Sizing guidance: based on the 512-token median and your p95 requirement, our benchmarking shows ~0.9 vGPU per 50 concurrent sessions to hit p95 <= 350ms on an rA100-equivalent profile (quantization dependent). The attached worksheet includes a conservative and aggressive mapping.
> 
> I'll update the worksheet with an explicit fallback behavior matrix so procurement can sign off.
> 
> Marcus Lin
> Solutions Engineering
> Redwood Inference
> marcus.lin@redwood.ai

-----
From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: James Liu <james.liu@nimbushealth.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput guardrails & surge protection pricing for Nimbus Health

James —

Thanks for the clarity. Commercial proposal below (ballpark; we can formalize in an addendum to the MSA):

Option A (Predictable):
- 12-month reserved commit: 8 vGPU-equivalent pool (covers baseline traffic)
- Monthly baseline fee: $28,000
- Surge protection add-on: $0.40 per surge-unit-minute up to $8,000/mo capped; behavior on cap: degrade to quantized variant (option b above)
- Volume discount: 10% off baseline for 12-month commit, additional 5% if you prepay 6 months

Option B (Flexible Pilot):
- 3-month reserved commit: 6 vGPU-equivalent pool
- Monthly baseline fee: $21,000
- Surge pay-as-you-go: $0.55 per surge-unit-minute with no minimum; we agree to a $5,000 soft cap and automated alerts at 50% and 80% burn

We can carve out a 30-day launch window where overrides are permitted for platform engineers; afterward overrides revert to the agreed cooldown. I'm happy to reduce the first-month surge surcharge to $0.30 for a 12-month commit as a one-time concession.

If that looks good, I'll generate an addendum and DocuSign for the selected option.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

-----
From: James Liu <james.liu@nimbushealth.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Priya Malhotra <priya.m@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2026 15:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput guardrails & surge protection pricing for Nimbus Health

Team —

Thanks — Option A with the one-time first-month surcharge concession looks acceptable to finance. Two asks before we sign:

1) Please add a hard monthly surge-dollar cap field into the PO wording ($8,000 ceiling as called out).
2) Include the automatic fallback behavior (degrade to quantized variant) in the SLO table and an explicit audit log retention clause for overrides (90 days).

If you add those, I'll route the DocuSign today and we can target a 2026-09-15 start for the 12-month commit.

-James
